faq.q: What time does the Marbella fishing and sunset combo charter 2033 start?
faq.a: The charter typically departs at 10:00 from Puerto Banús and returns at 18:00. This gives you a full 8 hours on the water – fishing the Mediterranean in the morning and early afternoon, then cruising back toward Marbella as the sun sets over La Concha.

faq.q: Do I need a fishing license for this charter?
faq.a: No. The boat holds a commercial fishing permit, so you can fish without an individual license. Our skipper will help with bait, rigs, and basic techniques – perfect if you've never fished before.

faq.q: Which boats can I book for the combo charter?
faq.a: The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are the most popular choices. Both depart from Puerto Banús and are equipped for comfortable day trips. For larger groups, ask about the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Mangusta 80 via WhatsApp.

The price covers the full 8-hour charter, a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, and Spanish IVA (21%). Fishing gear (rods, reels, bait, lures) is also included. There are no extra costs.

faq.q: What fish can I catch off Marbella?
faq.a: Common catches include sea bream, dentex, mackerel, and bonito. In summer, you might hook amberjack or even small tuna. The skipper knows the best spots near Cabopino and Cala del Faro. Catch-and-release is encouraged, but you can keep what's legal.

faq.q: Is the sunset cruise part of the same trip?
faq.a: Yes. After fishing, we head back toward Marbella's coastline, passing the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina. You'll watch the sun dip behind La Concha mountain while sipping cava or beer. It's a seamless transition from action to relaxation.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food or drinks?
faq.a: Absolutely – you're welcome to bring extra snacks or a picnic. The boat provides a cooler and ice. Just note that all standard drinks (soft drinks, beer, wine, cava) are already included, so you don't need to bring those.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faq.a: Your safety comes first. If strong winds or rough seas are forecast, we'll contact you to reschedule or offer a full refund. The skipper monitors conditions closely and will only sail if it's safe and comfortable.

data.body_html:
Combine the thrill of deep-sea fishing with the romance of a sunset cruise on this Marbella fishing and sunset combo charter 2033. Departing Puerto Banús at 10:00, you'll spend the morning chasing sea bream, dentex, and bonito off the Costa del Sol, then cruise back along the coast as the sky turns gold over La Concha. It's a full 8-hour day on the water – and one of the most memorable ways to experience Marbella.

How the Marbella Fishing and Sunset Combo Charter 2033 Works

This is a single, uninterrupted 8-hour charter – not two separate trips. You leave Puerto Banús at 10:00, head toward fishing grounds near Cabopino or Cala del Faro, and fish until around 14:00–15:00. Then the skipper turns the boat toward Marbella's coastline, and you enjoy a slow cruise past the Golden Mile, Marbella Marina, and the foothills of La Concha as the sun sets. You return to Puerto Banús at 18:00.

All gear – rods, reels, bait, lures – is provided. No fishing license needed. The skipper will show you the basics if you're new. Experienced anglers can bring their own tackle.

Which Boats Are Available for This Charter?

The combo charter is best suited to our Tier A yachts: the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax). Both depart from Puerto Banús, have spacious decks for fishing, and a shaded cockpit for relaxing. For larger groups (up to 12 pax), we can also arrange the Azimut 58 Flybridge or the Mangusta 80 – just ask via WhatsApp for pricing.

What's Included in the Price

The all-in price for the 8-hour charter is €2,299 (for Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39). This covers:

  • Licensed skipper and crew
  • Fuel for the full day
  • Fishing gear (rods, reels, bait, lures)
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21% VAT)

No hidden costs. The only things you might want to bring are sunscreen, a hat, and a camera for the sunset.

Fishing Grounds: Where You'll Fish

Your skipper will choose the best spot based on wind, tide, and season. Common areas include:

  • Cabopino – rocky seabed, good for sea bream and dentex
  • Cala del Faro – deeper water, mackerel and bonito in summer
  • Estepona coast – a longer run, but often produces larger fish

Don't expect trophy marlin – this is Mediterranean inshore fishing. But you'll almost certainly catch something, and the crew will clean and fillet your catch if you want to take it to a restaurant.

The Sunset Cruise: Marbella at Golden Hour

Around 15:00, the rods are stowed and the boat turns east. You'll cruise past the Golden Mile, Marbella Marina, and the old town, with La Con mountain rising behind. The skipper will cut the engine near Río Verde or Cala Cortés, letting you drift as the sun sinks into the sea. Cava is poured, music plays softly, and you watch the sky turn orange, pink, and violet. It's a quiet, luxurious end to an active day.

Who Is This Charter For?

This combo works for:

  • Families – kids love fishing, and the sunset part keeps everyone calm
  • Groups of friends – fish in the morning, party-lite in the afternoon
  • Corporate teams – team-building on the water, then networking at sunset
  • Couples – a unique date: catch your own dinner, then watch the sunset

No fishing experience is required. The skipper handles everything – you just show up and enjoy.

How to Book Your Marbella Fishing and Sunset Combo Charter 2033

Ready to secure your date? Browse all our Marbella boat charters or contact us directly via WhatsApp. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially from June to September. Payment is secure, and we'll confirm your skipper, boat, and departure time within 24 hours.
